notes_for_editor: Thin station: three sources read (the Coast Guard Light List 2025 copy, The Lighthouse Hunters, Lighthouse Digest). The Light List confirms position, characteristic and range; it does not give a first-lit date. Units: the Light List extract prints the range (11) without a unit, and the Lighthouse Hunters says 'miles'; the story says 11 with the source's wording, not nautical miles. The Digest gives Tower Height 35 with no unit printed; the story says 35 feet (11 m) and says so. The focal plane 141 is the Digest's figure; The Lighthouse Hunters gives 141 feet above the Pacific for the tower. The owners are named in the sources (Bill and Jo Ann Cady) and are not named in the story (private residents of a converted lighthouse; the rule in STORY_GUIDE). The story says 'the house was moved' because The Lighthouse Hunters says the owner moved his home; 'Curry County' appears in none of the three sources and is not used. Wikipedia gives first lit 1997 in its infobox and cites an NWcoast.com page (archived) and two travel and hiking pages; Wikipedia is a lead only and its 1997 date is not used. The NWcoast page was not read. The Oregon Coast Visitors Association page did not show its text in the cached read; a search snippet says first lit 1999 and 'not open to the public', but it was not read in full and is not cited. The Light List's LLNR is printed as 570 in the 2025 copy; the station record uses '6-0570'. The USCG navcen 2024 PDF returns 403; the 2025 copy at npshistory.com was used. The record's focal height 42.9 m matches the 141 ft figure. Access: privately owned; the Digest lists it as not open to the public; the story does not suggest visiting.
